deckName: KS3 DT · J1 Lesson 6 — Inside the Machine (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Lesson 6 · Inside the Machine
slides.sub: You are the surgeons. A computer is the patient. — J1 · Lesson 6 of 17
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: coming in, sitting beside their partner, logging in.

SAY: welcome them in. Today they take a computer apart and put it right.

WHEN TO MOVE: when most pupils are logged in, stop the room. Eyes front.

slides.heading: In this lesson you will…
bullets: Name the seven main parts inside a computer from their photographs.
Say the job of each part in one plain sentence.
Say what goes wrong when a part is missing, and which part a broken computer needs.
slides.notes:
SAY: read the three lines slowly. The third is the one that matters most.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: Scrub in
bullets: You work in a pair, on two laptops.
One of you is Dr Marmalade. The other is Dr Custard.
A computer lies on the table. It can talk.
Press Begin when your partner is there.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: eyes front, about to open the lesson.

SAY: read the four lines. If the class is an odd number, say that the last three work as a team of three. If the link between the two laptops is slow, the screen says: Share one laptop and take turns. That is fine.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in. The room now runs itself.

slides.heading: The operation
bullets: Click a part to take it out of the patient.
Listen to what the patient says.
Then click the job card that matches.
Take your time. Your patient will tell you.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: working in pairs on the operating table, for about eighteen minutes.

SAY: nothing, once they are in. Walk round and ask one question: what did the patient just say? Never tell them which card is right.

WHEN TO MOVE: when most pairs show the chart complete, move on. Pairs who finish early can operate on a second patient.

slides.heading: Ward round
bullets: Six broken computers are waiting for you.
Each one is missing one part.
Read what it says, then click the part it needs.
You have two tries on each one.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the operation is done. They now open the ward round on their own screens.

SAY: read the four lines. This is the same skill again, but now the patient is a computer in the real world.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in. About ten minutes.

slides.heading: Who is in charge?
bullets: You know the seven parts.
But someone has to tell them what to do.
Read the three lines on your screen.
Then answer one question on your own.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the ward round is finished. They open a short card with three lines and one question.

SAY: read the four lines. Say nothing more. The answer is on their screens and not on yours.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in. Five minutes.

slides.heading: Inside her head
bullets: Watch a short film. It has no sound.
Read the captions as it plays.
You can watch it again as often as you like.
Then you will put four steps in order.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: opening a film on their own screens, then a puzzle. About eight minutes in all.

SAY: read the four lines. If the film will not play for a pupil, show it on the board. Do not read out the steps.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in.

slides.heading: The names
bullets: You know the jobs. Now learn the real names.
Match each job to its name.
Place all seven, then check.
RAM, CPU, GPU and PSU are short names you will hear.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the film and the puzzle are done. They open the matching screen.

SAY: read the four lines. Do not say which name goes with which job.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in. Five minutes.

slides.heading: STOP — Exit check
bullets: Answer on your own now.
Your partner cannot help you.
Four questions about today.
Then finish How did it go? before you leave.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the names are matched. Eyes front for one minute.

SAY: read the four lines. Remind them these questions are marked and you can see every answer. Tell them the extra jobs are there for anyone who finishes early.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in. As they finish, put the last slide up.

slides.heading: Before you leave
bullets: Sign out properly. If you stay signed in, the next person to use this laptop can see your work.
Push your chair in. Tidy your area.
Today you took a computer apart and put it right.
Finish How did it go? before you go.
slides.notes:
SAY: end on the achievement. Six lessons in, they can now name every main part inside a computer and say what it does.

Before anyone leaves, check that every pupil has finished How did it go?
